citations.B1: Check-then-set race: two threads can both read the same count and both pass, admitting more than `limit`
citations.B2: Lost updates from the same race under-count real traffic, so the limiter is both leaky and inaccurate
citations.B3: guard with a lock or use an atomic INCR
citations.B4: No time window: counts never reset, so every user is permanently blocked after 100 requests; add a fixed/sliding window or token bucket keyed on time.
citations.B5: Unbounded memory: `counts` grows by one entry per distinct `user_id` forever; evict entries with a TTL or LRU.
citations.B6: Per-process state: each worker has its own `counts`, so the effective limit is `limit × workers`
citations.B7: No key validation: `None` or empty ids collapse all anonymous callers into one bucket, and unhashable ids raise
